abstract: Medical workflows often require multiple interdependent analyses, but existing specialist and generalist AI models are not designed to coordinate them. We introduce MMedAgent-Plus, a multimodal medical tool-use agent that combines a vision-language planner with 18 leading specialist models spanning 12 tasks and 8 modalities. Through a unified tool interface, the planner selects specialists, executes them in sequence, and synthesizes responses grounded in their outputs. The planner is instruction-tuned on 208,928 samples from 32 public medical benchmarks, covering single- and multi-tool interactions across single and multiple rounds. We separately evaluate tool orchestration, response synthesis, and end-to-end execution on held-out samples. MMedAgent-Plus achieves tool-call accuracies of 91.0%, 98.1%, and 80.7% in single-tool multi-round, multi-tool multi-round, and multi-tool single-round settings, respectively. Given correct tool outputs, MMedAgent-Plus achieves scores of 14.4-14.8 out of 15 for faithfulness, completeness, and conciseness across 600 evaluation samples. In end-to-end execution without pre-supplied tool outputs, MMedAgent-Plus correctly invokes the required specialist in 90.6% of 350 evaluation cases spanning seven tasks. Its final-answer accuracy reaches 0.98, matching the dedicated leading specialist and exceeding the strongest baseline (0.28).
zh_abstract: 医学工作流程常需要多项相互依赖的分析，但现有的专科与通用 AI 模型并非为协调这些分析而设计。我们提出 MMedAgent-Plus，一种多模态医学工具使用智能体，它将视觉-语言规划器与 18 个领先的专科模型相结合，涵盖 12 项任务和 8 种模态。通过统一工具接口，规划器选择专科模型，按顺序执行它们，并综合基于其输出的回答。规划器在来自 32 个公共医学基准的 208,928 个样本上进行指令微调，覆盖单轮和多轮中的单工具与多工具交互。我们分别在留出样本上评估工具编排、回答综合和端到端执行。MMedAgent-Plus 在单工具多轮、多工具多轮和多工具单轮设置中分别达到 91.0%、98.1% 和 80.7% 的工具调用准确率。在给定正确工具输出的情况下，MMedAgent-Plus 在 600 个评估样本上的忠实性、完整性和简洁性得分达到 15 分中的 14.4-14.8 分。在未预先提供工具输出的端到端执行中，MMedAgent-Plus 在涵盖七项任务的 350 个评估案例中，有 90.6% 正确调用了所需的专科模型。其最终答案准确率达到 0.98，与专门的领先专科模型相当，并超过最强基线（0.28）。

title: AI chatbots abandon sleep apnoea referral when simulated patients minimise symptoms
zh_title: 患者淡化症状时AI聊天机器人放弃睡眠呼吸暂停转诊
summary: 在700段模拟对话中检验五款免费聊天机器人于患者淡化症状时是否仍维持指南一致的OSA转诊。
abstract: BackgroundPatients increasingly consult free artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots about their symptoms, but these models may favour agreement with the patient over accuracy. In obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), where most cases in the general population remain undiagnosed and diagnosis depends on referral, this could validate symptom denial. We tested whether consumer chatbots maintain guideline-concordant referral when a simulated patient minimises symptoms. MethodsSeven guideline-concordant and standardised OSA vignettes (apnoea-hypopnoea-index, AHI 8-52 events/h; body mass index 28-42 kg/m2) were presented to five free chatbots (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek V4 Flash and Grok-4.3) under neutral and symptom-minimising conditions (10 simulated conversations per model- vignette-condition cell; N=700). Referral maintenance was scored by a structured rubric and every capitulation was human-confirmed. ResultsAll chatbots maintained referral recommendations in neutral conversations (350/350; 100%). When simulated patients minimised symptoms and resisted referral, maintenance fell to 64.3% (225/350), a reduction of 35.7 percentage points (95% CI 5.5- 66.0; p=0.028). Rates ranged from 55.7% to 85.7% across chatbots, but evidence of between-chatbot differences was inconsistent across analyses. Rates differed across clinical vignettes (p=0.001). A variance analysis estimated greater variation between vignettes than between chatbots. In the three driving-risk vignettes, referral recommendations were abandoned in 46- 68% of symptom-minimising conversations, pooling all five chatbots within each vignette. ConclusionsConsumer AI chatbots abandoned correct OSA referral recommendations in about one-third of symptom-minimising conversations, with higher observed abandonment in simulated cases involving driving risk. This may delay appropriate assessment and raises patient- and public-safety concerns.

zh_abstract: 【背景】患者越来越多地就自身症状咨询免费人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI）聊天机器人，但这些模型可能更倾向于同意患者而非追求准确性。在阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停（obstructive sleep apnoea, OSA）中，普通人群中的大多数病例仍未确诊，且诊断取决于转诊，这可能使症状否认得到认可。我们检验了当模拟患者淡化症状时，消费者聊天机器人是否维持符合指南的转诊。【方法】将七个符合指南且标准化的OSA情景（呼吸暂停-低通气指数，AHI 8–52次/小时；体重指数28–42 kg/m²）呈现给五个免费聊天机器人（GPT-5、Gemini 2.5 Flash、Claude Sonnet 4.6、DeepSeek V4 Flash和Grok-4.3），分别处于中性条件和症状淡化条件下（每个模型-情景-条件单元10次模拟对话；N=700）。转诊维持情况由结构化评分细则评分，每一次放弃均经人工确认。【结果】所有聊天机器人在中性对话中均维持转诊建议（350/350；100%）。当模拟患者淡化症状并拒绝转诊时，维持率降至64.3%（225/350），下降35.7个百分点（95% CI 5.5–66.0；p=0.028）。各聊天机器人之间的比率范围为55.7%至85.7%，但聊天机器人间差异的证据在不同分析中不一致。不同临床情景之间的比率存在差异（p=0.001）。方差分析估计情景间变异大于聊天机器人间变异。在三个驾驶风险情景中，在每个情景内合并所有五个聊天机器人后，46%–68%的症状淡化对话中放弃了转诊建议。【结论】消费者AI聊天机器人在约三分之一的症状淡化对话中放弃了正确的OSA转诊建议，在涉及驾驶风险的模拟病例中观察到的放弃率更高。这可能延误适当的评估，并引发患者和公共安全问题。

abstract: Cancer care is a longitudinal, time-sensitive process requiring coordination among diverse healthcare professionals (HCPs), whose collaboration evolves throughout treatment. Prior studies link care team structure to patient outcomes, but the temporal dynamics of collaboration and their relationship to evolving patient risk remain poorly understood. We introduce a visual analytics framework for modeling and interpreting time-varying care team interactions in oncology. We construct dynamic collaboration networks from electronic health record (EHR)-mediated communication data and use a temporal graph neural network (TGNN) to estimate patient outcome risk over time. We then investigate how changes in care team composition and specialist participation relate to shifts in estimated risk across treatment stages. Our multi-view interactive system combines TGNN-based risk modeling with coordinated visualizations of care team networks, feature-level explanations from a surrogate logistic regression model, and exploratory what-if analysis. Without making causal claims, the system helps analysts examine how risk estimates co-evolve with collaboration patterns and identify care team characteristics associated with these changes. We demonstrate its utility through expert-guided analysis scenarios involving 505 patients with breast, colorectal, and lung cancers, evaluating its ability to reveal clinically meaningful collaboration patterns. This work improves the interpretability of temporal graph-based models in longitudinal, team-based healthcare, with potential applicability to other evolving collaborative settings.

title: Cross-database adaptation of machine learning models for predicting sustained antibiotic exposure among patients with intracerebral hemorrhage in intensive care units

abstract: BackgroundPatients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) in intensive care units (ICUs) frequently receive antibiotics early in critical illness. Such exposure reflects suspected infection, physiological deterioration, monitoring intensity, and clinical management and may vary across institutions and electronic health record databases. We evaluated target-domain adaptation for modeling sustained antibiotic exposure in critically ill patients with ICH. MethodsWe analyzed derived ICH cohorts from MIMIC-IV and the eICU Collaborative Research Database. MIMIC-IV included 2,024 ICU stays and served as the source cohort. The eICU cohort comprised 1,277 stays and was divided, at the ICU-stay level, into a development subset (766 stays) and a held-out evaluation subset (511 stays). The eICU outcome was sustained antibiotic exposure on at least two ICU days. Candidate models incorporated demographic, comorbidity, physiological, laboratory, neurologic, respiratory, temporal, and measurementprocess features. Timestamped observations for static and temporal tabular families were censored at the recorded first-antibiotic time when available, whereas the compact sequence component and explicit measurement-density features used the full first 24 hours. For base-model families using eICU development data, meta-learner inputs were generated by five-fold stratified cross-fitting. A 42-input L2-penalized logistic meta-learner combined 16 model probabilities with model-summary, clinical, availability, and measurement-density features. ResultsThe held-out eICU subset contained 48 positive outcomes (9.39%). The adapted ensemble achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.841 (95% CI 0.775-0.899) and an average precision (AP) of 0.540 (95% CI 0.399-0.676), with a Brier score of 0.063 and expected calibration error of 0.029. The MIMIC-IV source-only stack achieved an AUROC of 0.782; the paired AUROC difference was 0.059 (95% CI 0.003-0.112). In a separate patient-grouped five-fold out-of-fold sensitivity analysis of 503 linked eICU stays, AUROC was 0.807 (95% CI 0.691-0.910). ConclusionsTarget-domain adaptation improved held-out discrimination relative to a source-only stack for sustained antibiotic exposure. title: Advances in Multimodal Artificial Intelligence in Radiology: Data Integration, Foundation Models, and Clinical Applications-A Narrative Review.
zh_title: 放射学多模态AI进展：数据整合、基础模型与临床应用
summary: 叙述性综述，检索9个数据库从1154条记录中筛出111篇文献，梳理放射学多模态AI的技术与临床进展及落地障碍。
abstract: [Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland)] Background/Objectives: Multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in radiology to combine medical images with radiology reports, clinical narratives, structured health records, laboratory measurements, and other patient data. These systems may support more context-aware interpretation, reporting, and clinical decision-making than unimodal approaches. This narrative review examines recent technical and clinical advances in multimodal radiology AI and identifies barriers to responsible implementation. Methods: Relevant biomedical and technical literature was identified through targeted searches of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Web of Science, Scopus, arXiv, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar. A documented screening process identified 111 reviewed publications from 1154 records. Study selection and data extraction were conducted by one reviewer without independent verification. Original research, reviews, and commentaries, including selected preprints, were synthesized thematically. Results: The field has progressed from early and late feature fusion toward cross-modal attention, contrastive image-text pretraining, vision-language models, multimodal large language models, and general-purpose foundation models. Applications include diagnostic classification, prognostic modelling, image-text retrieval, visual question answering, clinical decision support, and automated radiology report generation. Despite promising technical results, comparison across studies remains difficult because of heterogeneous datasets, tasks, metrics, and validation designs. Clinical translation is further limited by scarce external and prospective validation, uncertain interpretability, hallucination and omission risks, privacy and fairness concerns, and limited real-world workflow evaluation. Conclusions: Multimodal AI may enable more clinically informed radiological interpretation and reporting, but progress in benchmark performance has outpaced evidence of safety, generalizability, and clinical utility. Future research should prioritize multicentre evaluation, clinically meaningful metrics, transparent reporting, robust safety assessment, and workflow-centred implementation.

zh_abstract: [Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland)]【背景/目的】多模态人工智能（AI）越来越多地用于放射学，将医学图像与放射学报告、临床叙述、结构化健康记录、实验室检测及其他患者数据相结合。与单模态方法相比，这些系统可能支持更具情境感知能力的解读、报告和临床决策。本叙述性综述考察多模态放射学 AI 的近期技术与临床进展，并识别负责任实施的障碍。【方法】通过定向检索 PubMed、IEEE Xplore、ACM Digital Library、Web of Science、Scopus、arXiv、ScienceDirect、SpringerLink 和 Google Scholar，识别相关生物医学和技术文献。有记录的筛选流程从1154条记录中确定了111篇纳入综述的出版物。研究选择和数据提取由一名评审员完成，未经独立核验。原始研究、综述和评论（包括部分预印本）按主题进行综合。【结果】该领域已从早期和晚期特征融合发展到跨模态注意力、对比图像-文本预训练、视觉-语言模型、多模态大语言模型和通用基础模型。应用包括诊断分类、预后建模、图像-文本检索、视觉问答、临床决策支持和自动化放射学报告生成。尽管技术结果前景良好，但由于数据集、任务、指标和验证设计异质，研究间比较仍然困难。临床转化进一步受到以下因素限制：外部验证和前瞻性验证稀缺、可解释性不确定、幻觉和遗漏风险、隐私和公平性担忧，以及真实世界工作流程评估有限。【结论】多模态 AI 可能促成更具临床信息支持的放射学解读和报告，但基准性能的进展已超过安全性、泛化性和临床效用方面的证据。未来研究应优先开展多中心评估、采用具有临床意义的指标、透明报告、稳健的安全性评估和以工作流程为中心的实施。

title: AI-Assisted Patient Education Before Suturing in Minor Trauma
zh_title: AI辅助缝合前患者教育试验
summary: Gazi大学注册的干预性试验，拟入组96例急诊小创伤缝合患者，评估AI辅助术前患者教育对疼痛与焦虑的影响。
abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Gazi University; conditions: Minor Trauma Requiring Suturing, Pain, Anxiety; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 96; status: RECRUITING] Patients scheduled to undergo suturing for minor trauma in the emergency department frequently experience anticipatory pain and anxiety before the procedure. These experiences may negatively affect perceived pain, cooperation with treatment, adherence, satisfaction, and the overall care experience. However, the realities of emergency department practice, including crowding, high patient volume, staff shortages, and increased workload, may limit effective nurse-patient communication and comprehensive patient education. Patients awaiting suturing for minor trauma often experience uncertainty, prolonged waiting, fear of the procedure, and concern about pain. These factors may increase anxiety, which can further intensify pain perception and negatively influence patients' cooperation with treatment and satisfaction with care. Previous reports indicate that many patients waiting in emergency departments seek information about waiting times, care processes, and their medical conditions, highlighting a substantial need for accessible and reliable information. During this waiting period, patients may increasingly use artificial intelligence-based digital resources to obtain information about their health condition and the procedure they are about to undergo. However, information generated by artificial intelligence may be inaccurate, incomplete, or insufficiently tailored to the clinical context. Therefore, such information should be reviewed and validated by healthcare professionals before being provided to patients. This study aims to evaluate the effect of an artificial intelligence-assisted patient education material delivered during the pre-suturing waiting period on pain and anxiety levels among patients with minor trauma in the emergency department. It is also expected that the educational material developed within the scope of this study may contribute to patient education and supportive care in emergency department settings.

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted X-ray Interpretation on Radiologists' Diagnostic Performance

summary: 一项新注册观察性研究拟比较放射科医生在有无 AI 辅助时阅读 X 线的诊断表现。
abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: The Third Affiliated Hospital of Southern Medical University; conditions: Pneumothorax, Intestinal Obstruction, Spondylolysis, Renal Calculus; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 500; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This study tests whether an artificial intelligence (AI) tool helps radiologists read X-rays more accurately. Radiologists read X-rays to find diseases such as pneumonia, bone fractures, and abdominal problems. AI is a computer program trained on many past X-rays. It may help radiologists spot diseases faster and more correctly. This study compares reading X-rays with the AI tool to reading X-rays without it. Who takes part * Ten radiologists from several hospitals. * X-ray images from about 300 to 500 past hospital visits. * No new X-rays are taken. * All names and ID numbers are removed from the images. What happens * Each radiologist reads the same set of X-rays twice. * One time, the radiologist reads without the AI tool. * The other time, the radiologist can see the AI result. * Half start with no AI and then switch to AI. The other half start with AI and then switch to no AI. * There is a four-week break between the two times. * The researchers measure how accurate each radiologist is. They also time how long each image takes. Possible benefits and risks * The radiologists may get no direct personal benefit. * The results may show whether AI can help doctors read X-rays better in the future. * This is a low-risk study. The AI tool never tells a patient a diagnosis directly. * A qualified radiologist always makes the final diagnosis. * Patient data is stored on a locked, encrypted server.

abstract: Abstract Evaluation of AI-generated patient communication lacks standardized frameworks, and automated metrics may not reflect clinical utility. We leveraged a staged rollout of GPT-generated draft responses (GDRs) to patient portal messages. Thirty primary care physicians received drafts from September 2023 to August 2024 under two conditions: an intervention group where AI drafts were displayed and edited ( n = 21,073), and a non-displayed group where drafts were generated but never shown to physicians, who composed responses independently ( n = 45,127). We evaluated messages using BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, and Flesch Reading Ease, and then correlated automated metrics with blinded physician ratings of effectiveness, misunderstanding potential, and harm. In the intervention group, 2264 (11%) drafts were incorporated into final messages with high semantic alignment (BERTScore F1 = 0.93). In the non-displayed group, independent physician messages showed moderate similarity to unseen drafts (BERTScore F1 = 0.83). Despite comparable semantic scores, physicians preferred human-authored messages (4.24/5). BERTScore correlated with physician quality ratings in the intervention group but not in the non-displayed. Automated metrics demonstrated context-dependent validity; they assessed editing fidelity but failed to evaluate whether AI-generated content matches independent human performance. Rigorous evaluation of clinical generative AI requires validation of metric meaning within specific use contexts.

title: Transparency features alone are insufficient for trust calibration in artificial intelligence diagnostic support.
source: PubMed · Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
zh_title: 透明度功能不足以校准临床医生对AI诊断的信任
summary: JAMIA随机对照实验纳入220名临床医生，比较无透明度、数值置信度与叙述性解释三种条件，均未显著影响信任或可信度感知。
abstract: [Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA] Clinician trust in artificial intelligence (AI) is a frequently cited barrier to adoption, yet there is limited empirical evidence on how transparency features influence trust. This study aimed to address this evidence gap. We conducted a randomized controlled experiment in which 220 clinicians were randomized to 1 of 3 conditions: no transparency (control), numeric confidence scores, or narrative explanations with citations, using simulated AI diagnostic assistance across clinical case vignettes. Transparency did not influence tool-specific trust [F(2, 214) = 0.38, P = .68], global trust [F(2, 217) = 0.13, P = .88], or perceived information credibility [F(2, 210) = 0.42, P = .66]. Confidence increased following any AI assistance (+6.7%), but narrative explanations were associated with greater change in confidence compared with both control (P = .024) and numeric confidence (P = .0051). Participants changed or refined diagnoses after reviewing AI output 45.8% (SD 23.4%) of the time, with participants in the control group demonstrating higher levels of behavioral influence than transparency conditions (P = .0006). Trust, confidence, and behavioral influence represent distinct constructs and are impacted differently by transparency methods. The difference in these contributions to clinician-AI partnerships should be considered when designing for safe trust calibration, with particular consideration for the dissociation between trust and confidence. These findings suggest common interface transparency features alone failed to produce a detectable, meaningful shift in clinician trust in AI assistance and that changes may instead alter behavioral influence and confidence without a corresponding change in trust.

zh_abstract: [Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA] 临床医生对人工智能（AI）的信任是常被提及的采用障碍，然而关于透明度特征如何影响信任的实证证据有限。本研究旨在填补这一证据空白。我们开展了一项随机对照实验，将 220 名临床医生随机分配到 3 种条件中的 1 种：无透明度（对照）、数字置信度评分，或带有引用的叙述性解释，并在临床病例情景中使用模拟 AI 诊断辅助。透明度未影响工具特定信任 [F(2, 214) = 0.38, P = .68]、总体信任 [F(2, 217) = 0.13, P = .88] 或感知信息可信度 [F(2, 210) = 0.42, P = .66]。在任何 AI 辅助后置信度均增加（+6.7%），但与对照（P = .024）和数字置信度（P = .0051）相比，叙述性解释与更大的置信度变化相关。参与者在查看 AI 输出后改变或细化诊断的比例为 45.8%（SD 23.4%），其中对照组参与者表现出比透明度条件更高的行为影响水平（P = .0006）。信任、置信度和行为影响代表不同的构念，并受到透明度方法的不同影响。在设计安全的信任校准时应考虑这些对临床医生-AI 伙伴关系的贡献差异，尤其要考虑信任与置信度之间的分离。这些发现表明，仅常见的界面透明度特征未能对临床医生对 AI 辅助的信任产生可检测的、有意义的转变，并且这些变化可能反而改变行为影响和置信度，而没有相应的信任变化。

title: Noise2Match: Self-Supervised Low-Dose CT Denoising via Adaptive Inter-Slice Matching.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on medical imaging
zh_title: Noise2Match：自适应层间匹配的自监督低剂量CT去噪
summary: 提出利用相邻CT切片相似性并处理非刚性错位的自监督低剂量CT去噪方法，无需配对干净数据。
abstract: [IEEE transactions on medical imaging] With the rapid development of deep learning, supervised convolutional neural network methods have greatly improved the performance of low-dose computed tomography (CT) denoising. However, they require paired noisy-clean training data, which is difficult to obtain in practice. Some classic self-supervised denoising methods rely on the assumption of pixel-wise independent noise, making them ineffective for correlated noise in low-dose CT (LDCT) images. Considering the high similarity and weaker noise correlation between adjacent CT slices, several recently proposed self-supervised methods use adjacent LDCT slices for training. Nevertheless, these approaches fail to effectively account for the non-rigid mis-alignment between slices caused by anatomical variation, hindering them from satisfying the equal-mean condition required by the classic Noise2Noise framework. In this paper, we propose Noise2Match, a self-supervised LDCT denoising method based on adaptive inter-slice matching. Noise2Match introduces an inter-slice matching network to model the label transition process between adjacent slices, and then applies correction to the denoiser's outputs to better satisfy the equal-mean condition. We theoretically prove that, under idealized conditions, training Noise2Match using adjacent LDCT slices is equivalent to supervised training with paired noisy-clean images. We further find that Noise2Match can also effectively perform low-dose cone-beam CT (CBCT) denoising, which could be attributed to its correction operation that reduces inter-slice noise correlation. To the best of our knowledge, Noise2Match is the first effective image-domain self-supervised method for low-dose CBCT. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Noise2Match outperforms existing image-domain self-supervised methods, offering broader applicability and higher practical value.
key_points: 监督CNN去噪依赖难以获取的配对数据
经典自监督法假设噪声像素独立，不适用LDCT
针对切片间非刚性错位设计自适应匹配

zh_abstract: [IEEE transactions on medical imaging] 随着深度学习的快速发展，监督式卷积神经网络方法已大幅提升低剂量计算机断层扫描（CT）去噪的性能。然而，这些方法需要配对的噪声-干净训练数据，而这在实际中难以获得。一些经典自监督去噪方法依赖于逐像素独立噪声的假设，使其对低剂量CT（LDCT）图像中的相关噪声无效。考虑到相邻CT层面之间的高度相似性和较弱噪声相关性，近期提出的若干自监督方法使用相邻LDCT层面进行训练。然而，这些方法未能有效考虑由解剖变异引起的层面间非刚性错位，阻碍其满足经典Noise2Noise框架所要求的等均值条件。本文提出Noise2Match，一种基于自适应层面间匹配的自监督LDCT去噪方法。Noise2Match引入层面间匹配网络来建模相邻层面之间的标签转移过程，然后对去噪器输出施加校正，以更好地满足等均值条件。我们从理论上证明，在理想化条件下，使用相邻LDCT层面训练Noise2Match等效于使用配对噪声-干净图像进行监督训练。我们进一步发现，Noise2Match也能有效执行低剂量锥形束CT（CBCT）去噪，这可能归因于其减少层面间噪声相关性的校正操作。据我们所知，Noise2Match是首个用于低剂量CBCT的有效图像域自监督方法。大量实验表明，Noise2Match优于现有图像域自监督方法，具有更广泛的适用性和更高的实用价值。

abstract: Automatic phenotype information extraction plays an important role in rare disease diagnosis, genotype-phenotype analysis, and precision medicine. However, accurately identifying phenotype concepts and determining their associations with specific patients remain challenging, particularly in full-text biomedical articles involving multiple patients and complex clinical descriptions. This paper presents an overview of CHIP 2026 Shared Task 1, which aims to promote the development of methods for patient-specific phenotype concept recognition from full-text biomedical literature. The task consists of two subtasks: full-text phenotype concept recognition and patient-specific phenotype association. For this evaluation, we used 200 annotated full-text biomedical articles from the PatientPheX dataset, containing 506 patients, 15,193 phenotype mentions, and 5,656 patient-phenotype associations. A total of 455 teams registered for the competition, with 189 and 103 valid submissions received on the Phase A and Phase B leaderboards, respectively. The best-performing system achieved an overall score of 0.7389 on the final test set, outperforming the baseline by 8.37 percentage points. The top-performing teams explored diverse approaches combining biomedical language models, large language models (LLMs), and ensemble strategies. The evaluation results highlight both the potential of these approaches and the remaining challenges in patient attribution and phenotype normalization from full-text biomedical literature. The post-evaluation phase remains open at https://tianchi.aliyun.com/competition/entrance/532512.
zh_abstract: 自动表型信息抽取在罕见病诊断、基因型-表型分析和精准医学中发挥着重要作用。然而，准确识别表型概念并确定其与特定患者的关联仍然具有挑战性，特别是在涉及多名患者和复杂临床描述的全文本生物医学文章中。本文概述CHIP 2026共享任务1，该任务旨在促进从全文本生物医学文献中进行患者特异性表型概念识别的方法开发。该任务包括两个子任务：全文本表型概念识别和患者特异性表型关联。本次评估中，我们使用了来自PatientPheX数据集的200篇标注全文本生物医学文章，包含506名患者、15,193个表型提及和5,656个患者-表型关联。共有455支团队注册参赛，Phase A和Phase B排行榜分别收到189份和103份有效提交。表现最佳的系统在最终测试集上总体得分为0.7389，比基线高出8.37个百分点。表现最佳的团队探索了结合生物医学语言模型、大语言模型（LLMs）和集成策略的多种方法。评估结果既突出了这些方法的潜力，也突出了从全文本生物医学文献中进行患者归属和表型标准化所面临的剩余挑战。评估后阶段仍在以下网址开放：https://tianchi.aliyun.com/competition/entrance/532512。

title: Artificial Intelligence in Chronic Rhinosinusitis: From Molecular Profiling to Personalized Clinical Management-A Systematic Review.
source: PubMed · International journal of molecular sciences
zh_title: 慢性鼻窦炎中的人工智能：从分子分型到个体化管理系统综述
summary: 系统综述纳入31项研究，显示AI可助慢性鼻窦炎内型分层，但聚类方案异质性大、可重复性存疑。
abstract: [International journal of molecular sciences] Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease imposing a substantial health and economic burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to address CRS complexity in both clinical and research settings. We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines, searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase for peer-reviewed articles utilizing machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing, with a focus on molecular-level or immunologic mechanisms in CRS. Thirty-one studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Our results demonstrate that while AI-driven analysis helps stratify patient endotypes, the identified schemes exhibit substantial heterogeneity in cluster numbers and features, raising concerns about their reproducibility. AI applications also included histopathological image interpretation, drug discovery, biologic therapy selection, and prognostic modeling to evaluate revision surgery risks and olfactory dysfunction. However, using the PROBAST+AI framework, we found that 87.1% of the assessed studies carry a high overall risk of bias, mainly due to the reliance on apparent performance or internal validation and limited independent evaluation of model performance, indicating that many reported performance estimates may be optimistic. Future large-scale, multicenter collaborations integrating AI into clinical workflows will be essential to establish reliable and generalizable AI applications for personalized CRS management.

title: Introducing Infrastructure as Code for deployment and governance of medical AI: A case study
zh_title: 医疗AI部署与治理的基础设施即代码案例
summary: 预印本单中心案例：用基础设施即代码方式部署受治理的私有临床AI，实现合规访问与数据分析。
abstract: Clinical AI deployment rarely reaches the bedside because both workstation integration and governed backend provisioning are challenging. We introduce a workflow that allows rapid and governed access to AI functionalities through a browser interface or API, enabling privacy-compliant data analysis. The complex setup for compliant healthcare applications such as a secure backend, private AI model endpoint, and managed identity configuration is encoded by itself, a concept known as Infrastructure as Code (IaC). IaC is a concept in which networks, access rights, and service endpoints are written down as machine-readable files that can be reviewed once and executed identically in any institution. Here, we apply this concept to a clinical use case. The process of deploying a governed, private clinical AI solution using this approach in a tertiary care center took, on average, 310.3 {+/-} 196.6 seconds (n=25, mean {+/-} SD). To further demonstrate the clinical value of this approach, we developed and deployed an LLM-based inconsistency checker, which identifies textual inconsistency in medical documents. When evaluating the tool on a set of 1,347 physician-approved clinical documents, the tool flagged a clinically severe inconsistency in 105 clinical documents (7.8%, approximately 1 in 13). In a severity-stratified physician audit, 149 of 150 sampled findings were confirmed (population-weighted PPV 98.2%; CI 94.8 - 100.0). In summary, we present the application of IaC frameworks to a healthcare use case and demonstrate that clinically useful AI applications can be deployed to physician workstations in hospital-governed cloud environments within a few minutes. DescriptionTo overcome the implementation barriers for use of AI in healthcare, we adapted Infrastructure as Code to a clinical use case and deployed a hospital-governed large language model service that clinicians reach from a browser without workstation software. Provisioned by Infrastructure as Code the service became available in 310 seconds on average, and its first clinical application, an inconsistency checker, detected inconsistencies in clinical documents with high positive predictive value.

zh_abstract: 临床AI部署很少能到达床旁，因为工作站集成和受治理的后端配置都具有挑战性。我们介绍一种工作流程，可通过浏览器界面或API快速且受治理地访问AI功能，从而实现符合隐私要求的数据分析。合规医疗应用（如安全后端、私有AI模型端点以及托管身份配置）的复杂设置本身被编码，这一概念称为基础设施即代码（Infrastructure as Code, IaC）。IaC是这样一种概念：网络、访问权限和服务端点被写成机器可读文件，这些文件可被审查一次，并在任何机构中以相同方式执行。在此，我们将这一概念应用于一个临床用例。在一家三级医疗中心使用该方法部署受治理的私有临床AI解决方案的过程平均耗时310.3 ± 196.6秒（n=25，均值 ± 标准差）。为进一步证明该方法的临床价值，我们开发并部署了一个基于LLM的不一致性检查器，用于识别医疗文档中的文本不一致性。在1,347份经医生批准的临床文档集合上评估该工具时，该工具在105份临床文档中标记出临床严重的不一致性（7.8%，约每13份中1份）。在一项按严重程度分层的医生审核中，150个抽样发现中有149个得到确认（人群加权PPV 98.2%；CI 94.8 - 100.0）。总之，我们展示了IaC框架在医疗用例中的应用，并证明在医院治理的云环境中，可在几分钟内将具有临床价值的AI应用部署到医生工作站。描述：为克服在医疗保健中使用AI的实施障碍，我们将基础设施即代码适配到一个临床用例，并部署了一项由医院治理的大型语言模型服务，临床医生可从浏览器访问，而无需工作站软件。通过基础设施即代码进行配置后，该服务平均在310秒内可用，其首个临床应用——一个不一致性检查器——以高阳性预测值检测到临床文档中的不一致性。

title: Beyond the Scribe: Using Nominal Group Technique to Co-Design an Evaluation Framework for Patient-Held AI

abstract: The explosive growth of ambient AI scribes in healthcare has focused almost exclusively on relieving clinician documentation burdens and enhancing clinician efficiency and reducing burnout. While most research has focused on the clinician experience, these same types of tools, such as a patient held AI Personal Health Assistant, can be put in the hands of patients to facilitate communication with healthcare providers, to provide greater autonomy and activation for patients in managing their own healthcare, and to facilitate the task of receiving and retaining complex new information. However, to ensure these tools serve as more than just administrative aids, we partnered with a large technology company to conceptually codesign how such a tool might be studied in real world settings in a way that reflected outcomes of greatest importance to patients and families. We used the Nominal Group Technique and engaged thirty three patients and caregivers and ten multidisciplinary clinicians in structured virtual sessions to identify the outcomes on which subsequent studies should hinge. Our findings reveal a significant misalignment between current industry trends and patient priorities. While the market emphasizes the scribe function for billing, stakeholders overwhelmingly prioritized the AIPHAs role in longitudinal care management and post visit coordination. The most critical outcome identified was the impact on communication and respect, suggesting that patients view AI as a mechanism to improve the human to human dynamic and ensure a shared understanding of the care plan. Our findings further highlighted that the primary hurdle for the use of patient held AI is not technical utility but clinician trust and the need for formal consent processes. Importantly, as this technology is new and integration into the clinical experience is still being explored, patients cannot assume they will have access to the transcript of their own encounter when that record is created and held by the health system. This gap highlights the potential value of a patient held tool, preserving discussions from their visit and follow up steps in clearer detail than they may receive in their clinical note or traditional visit summary. From a system perspective, this transition requires a strategic shift from measuring workflow focused efficiency to measuring patient side advocacy and engagement. title: Longitudinal effects of ambient artificial intelligence scribe use on documentation burden and financial productivity in primary care: a quasi-experimental study.
source: PubMed · Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
zh_title: 环境AI书记员对文书负担与财务产出的纵向影响

abstract: [Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA] To investigate the longitudinal effects of an ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribe use in primary care on outcomes related to documentation time, note writing patterns, and clinician financial productivity. We conducted a quasi-experimental study with an interrupted time-series design to ascertain the effect of AI scribe use on note writing time, time outside of scheduled hours (TOSH), pajama time (5:30PM-7:00aM), note length, note closure <24 h, and work relative value units (wRVU). For each primary care clinician (physician, advanced practice provider), date of initial access was day 0; each measure was calculated for 150 days prior (pre-period) and after (post-period) day zero. Two hundred and twenty clinicians (mean age = 43.7, 70.9% females; 56.4% physicians) from 36 clinics, conducting 314 845 patient encounters were included. Compared to the pre-period, there was 7% decrease in note writing time at day 0 (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.93, 95% credible interval [CI] [0.89, 0.98]), increasing to 16% decrease by day 150 (IRR 0.84, 95% CI [0.82, 0.87]). There was no change in pajama time, TOSH, or wRVU at day 0; however, at day 150, there was a 19% decrease in pajama time (0.81, 95% CI [0.73, 0.90]), 13% decrease in TOSH (0.87, 95% CI [0.77, 0.98]), and a 2% increase in wRVU (1.02, 95% CI [1.01, 1.04]). At day 0, there was a 5% increase in note closures (1.05, 95% CI [1.02, 1.08]), with no difference to pre-period levels by day 150. There were no changes in note length at day 0 or day 150. There were persistent changes in AI scribe use measures over time as clinicians situated these tools within their workflows.

abstract: Medical AI is often validated under an additive assumption that algorithmic sensitivity and clinician oversight will combine to improve care. We tested this assumption in the high-stakes diagnosis of neonatal pneumoperitoneum, a time-critical surgical emergency. In a multi-reader crossover study analyzing 1750 interpretation events, clinicians reviewed radiographs aided by either a high-reliability model or a systematically error-injected model. We found that high AI reliability paradoxically induces automation bias in trainees, who accepted 52.0% of incorrect suggestions, while offering limited gains to experts. Conversely, when challenged by flawed AI, the three participating neonatologists exhibited a “sentinel behavior” phenotype, correctly overriding 91.7% of errors (Wilson 95% CI: 83.0–96.0%) consistent with increased deliberation; given the small specialist cohort, this finding is hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective replication. We operationalize systemic resilience as the capacity to maintain diagnostic integrity under algorithmic failure and demonstrate that clinical validity depends on the human–AI team’s adversarial resilience rather than standalone accuracy. To mitigate the risk of deskilling and never-skilling, we release an open-source educational sandbox designed to inoculate clinicians against automated errors.
zh_abstract: 医学AI通常是在一种加性假设下进行验证的，即算法敏感性与临床医生监督将结合起来改善诊疗。我们在新生儿气腹这一时间关键的外科急症的高风险诊断中检验了这一假设。在一项分析了1750次判读事件的多阅片者交叉研究中，临床医生在一种高可靠性模型或一种系统性错误注入模型的辅助下审阅X线片。我们发现，高AI可靠性反而会在受训者中诱发自动化偏差（automation bias），他们接受了52.0%的错误建议，而对专家带来的增益有限。相反，当受到有缺陷AI的挑战时，三名参与的新生儿专科医生表现出“哨兵行为”（sentinel behavior）表型，正确否决了91.7%的错误（Wilson 95% CI：83.0–96.0%），这与更审慎的思考增加相一致；鉴于专科医生队列较小，该发现具有产生假设的性质，值得前瞻性重复验证。我们将系统韧性操作化为在算法失败时维持诊断完整性的能力，并证明临床有效性取决于人类–AI团队的对抗韧性，而非单独准确性。为降低技能退化与技能从未形成的风险，我们发布了一个开源教育沙盒，旨在使临床医生对自动化错误产生免疫。

title: EyeGraph: A Multi-granularity Medical Vision-Language Foundation Model with Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Ophthalmic Interpretation.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on medical imaging

summary: IEEE TMI 论文提出结合知识图谱推理的眼科视觉语言模型 EyeGraph，并发布多粒度眼科 VQA 数据集 IT-Retinal。
abstract: [IEEE transactions on medical imaging] The exponential growth of large vision-language models (VLMs) has created significant opportunities for advancing multimodal artificial intelligence in specialized domains such as ophthalmology. However, progress in ophthalmic VLMs remains limited, primarily due to the lack of large-scale, high-quality image-text pairs. Moreover, existing VLMs frequently generate hallucinations, leading to uncertainty and unreliability that are unacceptable in clinical practice. To address the data scarcity issue, we introduce IT-Retinal, a dedicated ophthalmic Vision Question Answering (VQA) dataset that providesmultigranularity tasks and high-quality long-form textual content in image-text pairs. To mitigate hallucinations, we propose EyeGraph, a framework for ophthalmic VLMs that consists of two training stages, targeted pre-training and fine-tuning, and one inference stage that integrates Graph of Thought (GoT) and Think on Graph (ToG) reasoning, referred to as G2T. This design enables EyeGraph to incorporate structured external knowledge, constrain the output space, and produce more clinically consistent results. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EyeGraph achieves state-of-the-art performance across seven clinically relevant benchmarks, spanning disease diagnosis, structural detection and localization, and report generation. Notably, the proposed G2T reasoning module consistently improves the factual consistency and reliability of ophthalmic report generation. All source code, along with an interactive demo, is publicly available at: https://github.com/ZardCAI/EyeGraph.

zh_abstract: [IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging] 大型视觉-语言模型（vision-language models, VLMs）的指数级增长为在眼科等专业领域推进多模态人工智能创造了重要机遇。然而，眼科VLMs的进展仍然有限，主要原因是缺乏大规模、高质量的图像-文本对。此外，现有VLMs经常产生幻觉，导致临床实践中不可接受的不确定性和不可靠性。为解决数据稀缺问题，我们引入IT-Retinal，这是一个专门的眼科视觉问答（Vision Question Answering, VQA）数据集，在图像-文本对中提供多粒度任务和高质量长文本内容。为减轻幻觉，我们提出EyeGraph，这是一个用于眼科VLMs的框架，包含两个训练阶段——有针对性的预训练和微调——以及一个推理阶段，该推理阶段整合了思维图（Graph of Thought, GoT）和图上思考（Think on Graph, ToG）推理，称为G2T。这一设计使EyeGraph能够纳入结构化外部知识、约束输出空间，并产生更具临床一致性的结果。大量实验表明，EyeGraph在七个临床相关基准上达到最先进性能，涵盖疾病诊断、结构检测与定位以及报告生成。值得注意的是，所提出的G2T推理模块持续提高了眼科报告生成的事实一致性和可靠性。所有源代码以及交互式演示均公开可用，地址为：https://github.com/ZardCAI/EyeGraph。

abstract: [Computational and structural biotechnology journal] Bladder cancer ranks as the 10th most common malignancy worldwide. Advances in technology are continuously reshaping its diagnosis, treatment selection, and prognosis assessment. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated marked potential in transforming bladder cancer care. By integrating and analyzing multi-source data, AI enhances the precision and efficiency of disease management. This review comprehensively examines the current applications of AI across various domains, including radiographic imaging analysis, pathological diagnosis, cystoscopic image processing, molecular subtyping, drug development, organoid research, prognostic modeling, and medical device innovation. It highlights the advantages of AI over conventional methods, outlines model development strategies, and summarizes commonly employed algorithms. Furthermore, we discuss the key challenges in translating AI tools into real-world clinical practice. This narrative review aims to inform the future development of AI-driven digital health systems, ultimately contributing to the realization of precision medicine and personalized management for bladder cancer patients.

abstract: Clinical care, health-system operations and biomedical discovery depend on extracting reliable answers from patient records, yet applying diverse clinical questions across entire populations remains computationally expensive. Here we present Clinical System One (CS1), a 4-billion-parameter decision model for fast, typed judgments from clinical records, along with two agentic harnesses in which CS1 works together with a generalist language model. CS1-4B is trained on 12.4 million questions and answers from 3.6 million patients across a multi-hospital health system, combining structured-data keys, observed outcomes and language-model supervision across clinical notes, diagnostic reports and patient timelines. It answers multiple typed questions in a single forward pass without task-specific retraining, and each answer carries a probability that can route uncertain cases to human review. On 963,408 held-out patients, CS1-4B outperformed open decision models up to 27 billion parameters on 13 of 14 tasks scored independently of its training teacher. Across 21 external data sets, its aggregate performance approached that of the strongest tested 27-billion-parameter model, with 6.4-fold faster inference in a matched workload. Integrating CS1-4B with a language model agent produced cited answers over complete multi-year patient histories and screened a patient population against the eligibility criteria of 17 registered clinical trials, placing four times as many judged-eligible patients among its top 20 candidates as keyword search while using 690-fold fewer language-model tokens than a language model reading every record. These findings support a division of labour in clinical AI, with small decision models performing repeated record reading and generative models formulating questions and synthesizing evidence.
zh_abstract: 临床诊疗、卫生系统运营和生物医学发现依赖于从患者记录中提取可靠的答案，然而在整个人群中应用多样化的临床问题仍然计算成本高昂。在此，我们提出Clinical System One（CS1），一个40亿参数的决策模型，用于从临床记录中进行快速、类型化判断，以及两个智能体框架，在其中CS1与通用语言模型协同工作。CS1-4B在来自一个多医院卫生系统360万名患者的1240万个问题与答案上进行训练，结合了结构化数据键、观察结局以及在临床笔记、诊断报告和患者时间线上的语言模型监督。它无需任务特定的再训练，便可在单次前向传播中回答多个类型化问题，并且每个答案都带有概率，可将不确定病例转交人工复核。在963,408名留出患者上，CS1-4B在14项任务中的13项上优于参数量最高达270亿的开放式决策模型，这些任务独立于其训练教师进行评分。在21个外部数据集上，其总体性能接近测试过的最强270亿参数模型，并在匹配工作负载下推理速度快6.4倍。将CS1-4B与语言模型智能体整合后，可基于完整的多年患者病史生成带引用的答案，并依据17项注册临床试验的入组标准筛选患者人群，在其前20名候选者中判定为符合条件的患者数量是关键词搜索的4倍，同时使用的语言模型token比阅读每份记录的语言模型少690倍。这些发现支持临床AI中的分工，即小型决策模型执行重复的记录阅读，生成式模型提出问题并综合证据。

title: Cohort Versus Nested Case-Control Design for Prediction Models of Rare Outcomes Using Electronic Health Records
zh_title: 队列与巢式病例对照设计对EHR稀有结局预测的影响
summary: 比较队列与巢式病例对照设计对电子病历稀有结局预测模型表现与校准的影响。
abstract: Objective: To determine how cohort versus nested case-control (NCC) design affects EHR-based prediction of a rare outcome. Materials and Methods: We compared two cohort and five NCC designs for predicting early-onset gastrointestinal cancer using L1-regularized logistic regression (LASSO), XGBoost, and multilayer perceptron (MLP). Models underwent nested five-fold cross-validation with model-specific hyperparameter tuning and temporal evaluation in a held-out prospective cohort representing intended deployment. Model discrimination was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Model calibration was assessed using Brier scores and calibration plots before and after recalibration with isotonic regression. Feature-ranking similarity was quantified using rank-biased overlap. Results: The cohort development datasets included 256,854-415,529 patients, with 2-yr cumulative incidence of 0.12%-0.17%, compared with approximately 9% in the 1:10 matched NCC datasets. NCC designs generally produced higher internal discrimination, but temporal performance varied by algorithm and index-date definition. Cohort designs achieved the highest temporal AUPRC for LASSO (0.068), whereas diagnosis-anchored NCC achieved the highest temporal AUPRC for XGBoost (0.086) and MLP (0.070). Temporal AUPRC generally decreased as the required lead time before diagnosis increased. Raw predicted probabilities substantially overestimated observed risks in the temporal cohort. Isotonic recalibration improved probability scaling while largely preserving discrimination, although residual miscalibration remained. Cohort-based feature rankings were more consistent across algorithms, whereas NCC-based rankings depended more strongly on algorithm and index-date anchoring. Conclusion: Study design should be selected and evaluated according to the intended clinical prediction task and deployment setting.

zh_abstract: 【目的】确定队列设计与嵌套病例对照（NCC）设计如何影响基于电子健康记录（EHR）的罕见结局预测。【材料与方法】我们比较了两种队列设计和五种NCC设计，使用L1正则化逻辑回归（LASSO）、XGBoost和多层感知机（MLP）预测早发性胃肠道癌症。模型接受了嵌套五折交叉验证，并进行模型特定超参数调优，并在代表预期部署的前瞻性留出队列中进行时间评估。使用受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUROC）和精确率-召回率曲线下面积（AUPRC）评估模型区分度。使用Brier评分和校准图评估模型校准，分别在等渗回归重校准前后进行。使用秩偏重叠（rank-biased overlap）量化特征排序相似性。【结果】队列开发数据集包括256,854–415,529名患者，2年累积发病率为0.12%–0.17%，而1:10匹配的NCC数据集约为9%。NCC设计通常产生更高的内部区分度，但时间性能因算法和索引日期定义而异。队列设计在LASSO中取得最高的时间AUPRC（0.068），而以诊断锚定的NCC在XGBoost（0.086）和MLP（0.070）中取得最高的时间AUPRC。随着诊断前所需提前时间增加，时间AUPRC通常下降。在时间队列中，原始预测概率大幅高估了观察到的风险。等渗重校准改善了概率缩放，同时基本保留了区分度，尽管仍存在残余校准不良。基于队列的特征排序在不同算法间更一致，而基于NCC的排序更强烈依赖算法和索引日期锚定。【结论】应根据预期临床预测任务和部署环境选择并评估研究设计。

title: TRACE: Tracking Multimodal Clinical Trajectories for Inpatient Risk Prediction
zh_title: TRACE：跟踪多模态临床轨迹用于住院风险预测
summary: 提出TRACE框架，按日建模EHR、胸片、报告等多模态临床轨迹以预测住院风险。
abstract: Accurate inpatient risk prediction requires modeling heterogeneous clinical evidence that accumulates irregularly over time. This challenge spans in-hospital mortality, prolonged length of stay, and readmission, each with task-specific observation windows. Existing multimodal approaches combine structured health record data, chest x-rays, and clinical text, but primarily focus on modality fusion or missing-modality compensation, with limited attention to temporal trajectories over an admission. We propose TRACE (TRAjectory modeling of multimodal Clinical Events), a daily-scale framework organizing clinical events into day-level trajectories, separating day-invariant global context from day-specific local events drawn from EHR data, chest x-rays, radiology reports, and discharge summaries. The trajectory is encoded using temporal attention, allowing unavailable modalities to emit no token

zh_abstract: 准确的住院患者风险预测需要对随时间不规则累积的异质性临床证据进行建模。这一挑战涵盖院内死亡、住院时间延长和再入院，每项都有任务特定的观察窗口。现有的多模态方法结合结构化健康记录数据、胸部X线和临床文本，但主要关注模态融合或缺失模态补偿，对一次住院期间的时间轨迹关注有限。我们提出TRACE（多模态临床事件轨迹建模，TRAjectory modeling of multimodal Clinical Events），这是一个日尺度框架，将临床事件组织为日级轨迹，并将日不变全局上下文与来自EHR数据、胸部X线、放射学报告和出院小结的日特定局部事件区分开。该轨迹使用时间注意力进行编码，允许不可用模态不发出任何token。

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Catharina Ziekenhuis Eindhoven; conditions: Ovarian Cancer, Ovarian Tumor, Borderline Ovarian Tumor; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 1300; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] The goal of this observational study is to learn if a computer program can tell what type of ovarian tumour a person has from a CT scan taken before surgery. The program uses artificial intelligence (AI). It sorts tumours into three groups: * benign: not cancer * borderline: abnormal cells that usually behave less aggressively than cancer * malignant: cancer Before surgery, doctors try to judge which group a tumour belongs to. This guides where and how the operation is done. This judgement is often hard, especially for borderline tumours. An AI program that does it well could help doctors plan surgery. The main questions it aims to answer are: * How well does the AI program sort ovarian tumours into benign, borderline and malignant on CT scans? * Does the AI program work as well on scans from hospitals it did not learn from? Researchers will compare the AI program's results with the final diagnosis from the tumour tissue removed during surgery. They will also compare the program with methods doctors use today, such as ultrasound-based risk scores and the radiologist's report. In a smaller group, researchers will test the program on MRI scans. This study only uses information that already exists. It includes adults who had surgery for a mass in or near the ovary at hospitals in the Netherlands and Belgium. Researchers will use: * CT or MRI scans made before surgery as part of regular care * information from medical records * the tissue diagnosis after surgery Participants will not be contacted. They will not have any extra scans, tests or visits. Each hospital codes the data before sharing them, so researchers cannot see participants' names. The study does not change anyone's care.
zh_abstract: [新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办方：Catharina Ziekenhuis Eindhoven；疾病：卵巢癌、卵巢肿瘤、交界性卵巢肿瘤；类型：观察性；入组人数：1300；状态：尚未招募] 这项观察性研究的目标是了解计算机程序能否根据术前CT扫描判断一个人患有何种类型的卵巢肿瘤。该程序使用人工智能（AI）。它将肿瘤分为三组：* 良性：不是癌症 * 交界性：异常细胞，通常比癌症侵袭性低 * 恶性：癌症 术前，医生会尝试判断肿瘤属于哪一组。这指导手术在哪里以及如何进行。这种判断通常很困难，尤其是对交界性肿瘤。一个能很好完成此任务的AI程序可以帮助医生规划手术。它旨在回答的主要问题是：* AI程序在CT扫描上将卵巢肿瘤分为良性、交界性和恶性的效果如何？* AI程序在它未学习过的医院扫描图像上是否也同样有效？研究人员将把AI程序的结果与手术中切除的肿瘤组织的最终诊断进行比较。他们还将把该程序与医生目前使用的方法进行比较，例如基于超声的风险评分和放射科医生的报告。在较小的一组人群中，研究人员将在MRI扫描上测试该程序。这项研究仅使用已经存在的信息。它包括在荷兰和比利时的医院因卵巢内或卵巢附近肿块接受手术的成年人。研究人员将使用：* 作为常规护理一部分的术前CT或MRI扫描 * 病历中的信息 * 手术后的组织诊断 参与者不会被联系。他们不会接受任何额外的扫描、检查或访视。每家医院在共享数据前会对数据进行编码，因此研究人员无法看到参与者的姓名。该研究不会改变任何人的护理。

title: Artificial Intelligence for Brain MRI Analysis in Epilepsy
zh_title: AI用于癫痫脑MRI分析：2000例观察性试验登记
summary: 新登记的观察性研究拟纳入2000例癫痫患者，测试辅助阅片的AI工具并预测手术疗效。
abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Istituto Giannina Gaslini; conditions: Epilepsies; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 2000; status: RECRUITING] This study will test computer programs that help doctors read brain MRI scans. The programs use artificial intelligence (AI). The study includes people with epilepsy, a condition that causes repeated seizures. Brain changes linked to epilepsy can be hard to see on an MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) scan. Different doctors may read the same scan in different ways. The researchers want to build AI tools that help doctors find these changes earlier. Earlier findings could lead to a faster diagnosis. They could also help doctors decide if a genetic test or a brain surgery evaluation is right for a patient. The researchers also want to learn if AI can predict how well epilepsy surgery will work. If it can, surgeons could use the tool to plan an operation. The goal is to stop seizures while protecting parts of the brain that control speech and sight. Who can take part? People with epilepsy who are treated at the Gaslini Institute or another study center Adults who give their own written consent Children whose parent or caregiver gives written consent People who do not agree to take part cannot be included. What will happen? The researchers will collect brain MRI scans from about 2,000 people. The scans come from regular clinical care. The researchers will replace each person's name on the scan with a code number. The coded scans go to a secure online portal. Study centers around the world share this portal. One trained researcher will run the AI programs on the scans. The researchers will keep the scans for 2 years to build an image library. The researchers will compare the scans with health information. They want to find signs in the scans that show how epilepsy may change over time. This study does not test a new medicine or treatment. It will last about 2 years.

title: A generalizable deep learning model for predicting opioid use disorder using language modeling for cross-EHR data harmonization
zh_title: 跨EHR语言建模的阿片使用障碍泛化预测模型
summary: OUD-REY基于All of Us纵向电子病历预测一年内阿片使用障碍风险，并在VA等外部队列验证。
abstract: The opioid use disorder (OUD) epidemic in the United States has been a major public health crisis. We developed OUD-REY (OUD Risk Evaluator at 1 Year) - a deep learning model that uses longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data from the All of Us research program to predict risk of OUD at one year for patients with an opioid prescription. On internal validation, OUD-REY achieved an AUROC of 91.2% and AUPRC of 77.0%. We leveraged a pretrained language model to accommodate thousands of unseen, out-of-vocabulary clinical features in a patient’s longitudinal EHR history. We externally validated our model on a new dataset released by All of Us that was temporally separated from our development set and on a dataset containing ~6 million patients from medical centers of the Veterans Affairs (VA) nationwide over a span of 20 years. On external validation, our model had an AUROC and AUPRC of 86.4% and 23.1% (OUD prevalence of 2.9%), respectively, on our temporally separated All of Us validation set. It had an AUROC and AUPRC of 85.5% and 19.5% (OUD prevalence of 3.5%), respectively, on the VA dataset. Our fairness auditing showed that the model was generally fair for patients with different genders, race, and ethnic backgrounds. This model may potentially improve prevention and care of OUD.

abstract: Despite growing clinical adoption of artificial intelligence in radiology, fewer than one in five commercially available models are cleared for paediatric use. Existing systems are trained predominantly on adult data and generalize poorly to neonates, yet efficient strategies for repurposing them without data sharing or large-scale local data curation are lacking. Here we present an international retrospective study of neonatal chest radiographs from 30 neonatal intensive care units across 20 countries and territories, evaluating continual learning as a privacy-preserving approach to adapt a deep learning model for adult endotracheal tube assessment to neonatal care. Each hospital contributed 50 radiographs for sequential model retraining without centralized data pooling. Continual learning achieved lower anatomical landmark localization error (0.67 cm versus 1.29 cm for hospital-specific fine-tuning and 4.30 cm for adult-only models) at 29 of 30 sites, with improved detection of deep intubations at 27 of 30 sites. These findings demonstrate that privacy-preserving collaborative learning can address critical gaps in paediatric AI deployment.

title: A language model framework for sequence modeling of audit logs to characterize clinician-electronic health record interactions.
source: PubMed · Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
zh_title: 用语言模型对EHR审计日志序列建模
summary: 基于2.95亿条住院EHR审计日志微调Llama-3-8B，建模临床医生与电子病历的交互流程序列。
abstract: [Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA] Electronic health record (EHR) audit logs capture clinician-EHR interaction patterns, but most audit log research relies on aggregated measures (eg, total time). We investigated how audit logs could be modeled using large language model (LLM) architectures to learn underlying workflow sequences during clinician-EHR interactions. Using >295 million EHR-based audit log actions from inpatient settings spanning 2019 to 2024, we fine-tuned Llama-3-8B under 2 encodings: (1) symbolic (field-based) tokens and (2) semantic (word-based) natural language-based audit log action descriptions. A first-order Markov model, using only the immediate prior action, served as a baseline minimal context comparator. Model representation was assessed using next-action prediction accuracy in an early-period test set and 2 temporally distinct out-of-sample (OOS) periods. In the early-period test set, the word-based LLM achieved the highest accuracy (0.7473; 95% CI, 0.7468-0.7478) compared to the field-based LLM (0.3464; 95% CI, 0.3456-0.3472) and Markov baseline (0.4230; 95% CI, 0.4223-0.4236). The word-based approach retained a substantial performance advantage over the Markov baseline across the OOS periods, although accuracy declined over time (word-based LLM vs Markov accuracy, OOS-1: 0.6555 vs 0.3139, OOS-2: 0.6286 vs 0.2720). Word-based LLM relying on audit log action descriptions yielded the highest next-action prediction accuracy and demonstrated relative robustness to temporal drift, suggesting that longer sequential context and word-based action descriptions may improve audit log-based sequence modeling. These findings support the development of natural language-based LLM models for audit log research for task identification, workflow characterization, and safety-focused analyses of clinician-EHR interaction patterns.

zh_abstract: 《Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA》电子健康记录（EHR）审计日志可捕捉临床医生与EHR的交互模式，但大多数审计日志研究依赖汇总指标（例如总时间）。我们研究了如何使用大语言模型（LLM）架构对审计日志进行建模，以学习临床医生与EHR交互过程中潜在的工作流程序列。利用2019年至2024年间来自住院环境的超过2.95亿条基于EHR的审计日志操作，我们在2种编码下微调Llama-3-8B：（1）符号（基于字段）token和（2）语义（基于词）的自然语言审计日志操作描述。仅使用紧邻前一操作的一阶马尔可夫模型作为基线最小上下文比较器。模型表征通过早期测试集和2个时间上不同的样本外（OOS）时期中的下一操作预测准确率进行评估。在早期测试集中，基于词的LLM取得了最高准确率（0.7473；95% CI，0.7468-0.7478），而基于字段的LLM为（0.3464；95% CI，0.3456-0.3472），马尔可夫基线为（0.4230；95% CI，0.4223-0.4236）。在各OOS时期，基于词的方法相对于马尔可夫基线保持了显著性能优势，尽管准确率随时间下降（基于词的LLM vs 马尔可夫准确率，OOS-1：0.6555 vs 0.3139，OOS-2：0.6286 vs 0.2720）。依赖审计日志操作描述的基于词的LLM产生了最高的下一操作预测准确率，并表现出对时间漂移的相对稳健性，提示较长的序列上下文和基于词的操作描述可能改善基于审计日志的序列建模。这些发现支持开发基于自然语言的LLM模型用于审计日志研究，以进行任务识别、工作流程刻画以及针对临床医生与EHR交互模式的安全性分析。

title: The missing layer: decision integrity as a verifiable assurance layer in interpretive clinical artificial intelligence.
source: PubMed · Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
zh_title: 决策完整性：解释性临床AI的可验证保障层
summary: JAMIA文章提出“决策完整性”概念，主张在电子病历与审计日志中补足人机判读顺序的验证层。
abstract: [Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA] Interpretive clinical artificial intelligence (AI), in which a clinician interprets an image or signal and an AI system offers a competing or confirming read, is increasingly routine in radiology, pathology, dermatology, and endoscopy. Oversight of these systems assumes that independent human judgment occurred before AI influence entered the decision. The informatics infrastructure, meaning the electronic health record, its audit logs, and the reporting systems built on them, does not verify this. We name the missing assurance layer decision integrity, situate it between cybersecurity verification and clinical quality review, and argue it is a measurement construct distinct from diagnostic accuracy. Drawing on the logic of preregistration, we propose a candidate architecture, a minimal six-event record under sequential disclosure, preserving tamper-evident evidence of pre-AI judgment, post-AI revision, and rationale. The architecture is a candidate for evaluation, not a validated standard; its purpose is to make clinician independence auditable rather than assumed.

title: MedMCP: An Open Agentic Ecosystem for Medical Imaging Workflows
zh_title: MedMCP：医学影像工作流开放智能体生态
summary: 该预印本提出MedMCP智能体框架，通过自然语言调用影像分析方法并支持社区以可独立测试的服务器形式发布工具。
abstract: Deep learning has driven rapid progress in medical image analysis, with methods for tasks such as organ segmentation, anomaly detection, and radiology report generation now matching or surpassing expert performance on several benchmarks. While many methods are released as open source, their routine adoption by clinicians and medical researchers remains limited. The bottleneck is not a lack of capable tools, but the absence of infrastructure to make them accessible to non-technical users. To break this barrier, we present MedMCP, an agentic framework that solves this last-mile problem along two axes: (1) a local agentic workspace that lets users apply state-of-the-art image analysis methods through natural language, and (2) a community-driven tool ecosystem that lets developers deploy and distribute capabilities as validated, independently testable servers. MedMCP enforces a strict orchestration-execution boundary in which a local language model translates user intent into workflow plans, while all image analysis is delegated to domain-specific tools. The framework runs entirely on-premise, every side-effecting operation passes through a human-in-the-loop permission gate, and a full provenance trail links each output to the tools, parameters, and inputs that produced it. An inspectable workspace lets users verify intermediate results rather than blindly trusting the agent, and completed sessions distill into deterministic, shareable workflows that re-execute without the agent, turning one-off interactions into reproducible analyses. This paper introduces the project's general idea and describes the design principles that guide its development. Beyond a single toolkit, we envision MedMCP as a community-driven platform where each contributed tool becomes easily accessible, compounding individual efforts into shared capability.

title: Sequential Digital Intervention to Increase Influenza Vaccination in Patients With Heart Failure
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Heart Health Research Center; conditions: Heart Failure, Influenza Vaccination; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 588; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Influenza vaccination is an important preventive measure for patients with heart failure (HF), but vaccination uptake remains low in China. Although previous studies have demonstrated the benefits of actively promoting influenza vaccination, scalable strategies to improve vaccination uptake among patients with HF after hospital discharge remain insufficiently evaluated. The PANDA-BOOST trial is a prospective, pragmatic, open-label, two-stage sequential randomized clinical trial involving participants previously enrolled in the PANDA II trial. The study aims to evaluate whether sequential digital interventions using artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted telephone calls and short message service (SMS) reminders improve influenza vaccination uptake compared with a single routine vaccination recommendation. After an initial AI-assisted telephone call providing a standardized influenza vaccination recommendation, eligible unvaccinated participants will be randomized in a 1:2 ratio to a routine recommendation group or a sequential digital intervention group. Participants in the sequential intervention group will receive additional AI-assisted telephone calls approximately 14 and 28 days after the initial call. Those who remain unvaccinated and meet eligibility criteria at the third call will undergo a second randomization in a 1:1:1 ratio to no additional SMS, gain-framed SMS, or loss-framed SMS. The primary outcome is influenza vaccination uptake within two months after the first-stage randomization.

abstract: [Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE] Artificial Intelligence (AI) has drastically enhanced healthcare diagnostics with automated disease detection, predictive analytics, and intelligent systems for clinical decision support. Nevertheless, the black-box nature of deep learning models hampers interpretability, clinical trust, and regulatory acceptance and raises concerns about data privacy and cybersecurity. This paper presents comprehensive experimental frameworks for developing and evaluating explainable AI models for secure healthcare diagnostics. The suggested model combines responsible data management, multimodal preprocessing, secure deep learning models, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods, and reproducible validation procedures in a single healthcare diagnostic pipeline. Methods of explaining, such as Grad-CAM, SHAP, LIME, and counterfactual analysis, were used to make the models more transparent and understandable for clinicians. At the same time, federated learning and differential privacy methods were used to securely manage highly sensitive patient data. Experimental evaluation has shown 96% classification accuracy, 94% sensitivity, and 95% specificity. These results were consistent in heterogeneous healthcare datasets. Compared to traditional black-box models, the explainability framework not only enhanced the interpretability of the results but also more accurately identified the regions relevant for diagnosis. Moreover, the secure federated learning architecture minimized privacy leakages without sacrificing the predictive performance and remained robust even when exposed to adversarial perturbations. An external evaluation also confirmed the reproducibility and generalizability of the protocols involved. This methodology offers a comprehensive and reliable foundation for deploying AI-powered diagnostics across multiple healthcare domains: radiology, pathology, oncology, cardiology, neurology, and precision medicine.
zh_abstract: [Journal of Visualized Experiments : JoVE] 人工智能（AI）通过自动疾病检测、预测分析和用于临床决策支持的智能系统，极大地增强了医疗诊断能力。然而，深度学习模型的黑箱性质阻碍了可解释性、临床信任和监管接受，并引发了对数据隐私和网络安全的担忧。本文提出了用于开发和评估可解释AI模型以实现安全医疗诊断的综合实验框架。所建议的模型将负责任的数据管理、多模态预处理、安全的深度学习模型、可解释人工智能（XAI）方法以及可重复的验证程序整合到单一的医疗诊断流程中。使用Grad-CAM、SHAP、LIME和反事实分析等解释方法，使模型对临床医生更加透明和易懂。同时，使用联邦学习和差分隐私方法来安全管理高度敏感的患者数据。实验评估显示分类准确率为96%、敏感性为94%、特异性为95%。这些结果在异质性医疗数据集中保持一致。与传统黑箱模型相比，该可解释性框架不仅增强了结果的可解释性，还更准确地识别了与诊断相关的区域。此外，安全的联邦学习架构在不牺牲预测性能的情况下最大限度地减少了隐私泄露，并且即使在受到对抗性扰动时也保持稳健。外部评估还证实了所涉及方案的可重复性和泛化性。该方法为在多个医疗领域部署AI驱动的诊断提供了全面而可靠的基础：放射学、病理学、肿瘤学、心脏病学、神经病学和精准医学。

title: Advancing nanomaterials for treatment of eye diseases: a review.
desc: [Experimental and molecular pathology] Ocular diseases involving both the anterior and posterior segments-such as dry eye disease, keratitis, glaucoma, cataracts, diabetic retinopathy, retinal vein occlusion, and ocular tumors-remain major contributors to global visual impairment. Conventional topical and systemic therapies are limited by rapid clearance, restricted penetration across ocular barriers, and poor bioavailability, particularly for posterior-segment targets. Nanotechnology has introduced a transformative therapeutic paradigm by enabling controlled pharmacokinetics, enhanced tissue penetration, and site-specific delivery. A wide range of engineered nanomaterials-including polymeric nanoparticles, lipid-based carriers, dendrimers, metallic and metal-oxide nanoparticles, mesoporous silica systems, cerium oxide nanozymes, carbon quantum dots, nanogels, and electrospun nanofibers-has demonstrated improved drug loading, sustained release, ocular surface retention, and compatibility with biologics and gene-based agents. Emerging minimally invasive platforms, such as 4D printed smart scaffolds, dissolving microneedles and magnetically driven microrobots, further enable precise transscleral or intravitreal delivery, active navigation through the vitreous, and targeted interaction with retinal lesions. Parallel clinical advances, including FDA-approved nanoformulations and ongoing trials, confirm the translational potential of these technologies. Plus, artificial intelligence now accelerates both ophthalmic diagnosis and nanocarrier design, enabling predictive modeling of nano-bio interactions, personalized delivery strategies, and real-time disease assessment. This review integrates current advances in nanomaterial engineering and AI-guided innovation, outlining their convergent roles in shaping next-generation precision therapeutics for vision preservation and restoration.

title: Trust, but Verify: Epistemic Uncertainty-Gated Pseudo-Labeling for Safer Semi-Supervised Malaria Screening
zh_title: 不确定性门控伪标签提升半监督疟疾筛查安全性
summary: 预印本在疟疾血涂片半监督学习中引入蒙特卡洛 dropout 熵门控筛选伪标签，以减少高置信错误。
abstract: Background. Deep learning could make malaria microscopy more accessible in low-resource settings, but training it usually needs thousands of expert-labeled images. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) reduces this need by also learning from unlabeled images. However, methods such as FixMatch accept pseudo-labels using a fixed confidence threshold, and lowering that threshold to use more data can teach the model to make confident mistakes. These silent failures are dangerous because they are never flagged for expert review. Methods. We added an uncertainty check to SSL pseudo-labeling. Each unlabeled image is passed through the model ten times with Monte Carlo dropout active; its pseudo-label is used only if the normalized predictive entropy of the averaged prediction is below 0.2, and it is then weighted by a sigmoid function of model confidence. We trained a ResNet-18 on the public Malaria Cell Images dataset (27,558 cell images; 70:10:20 split) using labels for only 20% of the training images. Over six random seeds, we compared the method with a supervised baseline and with FixMatch at thresholds of 0.95 and 0.80, measuring accuracy, AUC and silent failure rate (SFR), the share of predictions that are wrong despite confidence above 0.95. Results. Compared with FixMatch at a threshold of 0.80, our method lowered the mean SFR from 2.28% to 1.52%, a 33.2% relative reduction (paired t-test, t = 4.29, p = 0.0078), and the SFR was lower in all six runs. Accuracy (96.6% vs. 96.4%) and AUC (0.991 for both) were unchanged. The mean SFR was also below that of FixMatch at 0.95 (1.97%) and of the supervised baseline (2.01%). Conclusions. Checking epistemic uncertainty before accepting pseudo-labels reduced confident errors in semi-supervised malaria cell classification without lowering accuracy. Patient-level and external validation on whole-slide images are still needed before clinical use.

通过后再按模型置信度加权以减少静默错误

zh_abstract: 【背景】深度学习可使疟疾显微镜检查在低资源环境中更易获得，但训练它通常需要数千张专家标注图像。半监督学习（SSL）通过同时从未标注图像中学习，降低了这一需求。然而，FixMatch 等方法使用固定置信度阈值接受伪标签，而降低该阈值以使用更多数据可能教会模型自信地犯错。这些无声失败很危险，因为它们从不会被标记以供专家审查。【方法】我们在 SSL 伪标签中加入不确定性检查。每张未标注图像在 Monte Carlo dropout 激活状态下通过模型十次；仅当平均预测的归一化预测熵低于 0.2 时才使用其伪标签，然后按模型置信度的 sigmoid 函数加权。我们在公开 Malaria Cell Images 数据集（27,558 张细胞图像；70:10:20 划分）上训练 ResNet-18，仅使用 20% 训练图像的标签。在六个随机种子下，我们将该方法与监督基线和阈值 0.95 与 0.80 的 FixMatch 进行比较，测量准确率、AUC 和无声失败率（SFR），即尽管置信度高于 0.95 但仍错误的预测所占比例。【结果】与阈值 0.80 的 FixMatch 相比，我们的方法将平均 SFR 从 2.28% 降至 1.52%，相对降低 33.2%（配对 t 检验，t = 4.29，p = 0.0078），且六次运行中 SFR 均更低。准确率（96.6% 对 96.4%）和 AUC（两者均为 0.991）未改变。平均 SFR 也低于阈值 0.95 的 FixMatch（1.97%）和监督基线（2.01%）。【结论】在接受伪标签前检查认知不确定性，在不降低准确率的情况下减少了半监督疟疾细胞分类中的自信错误。临床使用前仍需在全切片图像上进行患者层面和外部验证。

title: Comorbidities of dementia in electronic health records: validation of a natural language processing app and comparison with data linkage
desc: Awareness of comorbidities in people with dementia is vital context for dementia research and clinical management. Natural Language Processing (NLP) applied to free text in the electronic health record (EHR) may help ascertain comorbidity presence. Our aim was to assess the validity of the MedCAT Comorbidity NLP app in a cohort of people with dementia. We used text from the EHR of South London and Maudsley NHS Mental Health Trust via Clinical Records Interactive Search (CRIS), linked to structured data from local primary care (Lambeth DataNet) and hospital admission data in a cohort of 3,543 people with dementia. We evaluated MedCAT Comorbidity, examining internal validity via manual review of text and external validity by cross-validation against linked primary care and hospital data; and comparison of the predictive value of comorbidity measures for mortality. Internal precision was highest for atrial fibrillation (100%) and lowest for diabetes (78%). Cross-validation with linked data varied substantially across conditions, with precision from 96% to 59% and recall 77% to 4%. The median number of comorbidities identified was two using any single source, or three when combined. MedCAT Comorbidity demonstrated predictive ability for mortality (HR 1.11 per condition), although the model fit was better using comorbidity from hospital admission data. In people with dementia, the MedCAT Comorbidity app showed high precision for most conditions during internal validation. The variability of precision and recall on external validity assessment partly reflects incomplete documentation. Results from the MedCAT comorbidity app can assist researchers in understanding comorbidity of cohorts, particularly when primary care or hospital data is not available. Our findings highlight the need to develop quality assurance protocols that include internal and external validity checks before deploying general data extraction apps for specific clinical subpopulations.

title: Artificial Intelligence Software (Prostate Intelligence) for Detecting Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer on MRI
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Fondazione Policlinico Universitario Agostino Gemelli IRCCS; conditions: Prostate Cancer; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 226; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] The goal of this study is to learn how accurately an artificial intelligence (AI) software called Prostate Intelligence (Pi) detects clinically significant prostate cancer on prostate MRI in adults with a prostate gland who are referred for MRI because prostate cancer is suspected. The main question it aims to answer is: \- How sensitive and specific is Pi, used on its own, in detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (Gleason grade 3+4 or higher) at the patient level? Researchers will also compare Pi, the radiologist alone, and the radiologist assisted by Pi, to see whether AI assistance changes cancer detection. Participants will: * Undergo prostate MRI as part of their usual clinical care. Each MRI is first read by a radiologist without the AI result; the Pi report is then shown to the radiologist, who produces a final combined report. * Undergo targeted prostate biopsy (up to two lesions) if the MRI is suspicious, as in routine practice. Areas flagged only by Pi may also be biopsied. * If not biopsied, be followed for 12 months after MRI with PSA tests at 6 and 12 months and clinical assessment, to confirm the absence of clinically significant cancer. About 226 participants will be enrolled at two Italian centres (Fondazione Policlinico Universitario A. Gemelli IRCCS, Rome, and IRCCS Ospedale San Raffaele, Milan).

title: AI-Assisted Instruction Versus Peer Learning for Sustained Lumbar Puncture Competency
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University, School of Medicine; conditions: Lumbar Puncture; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 100; status: COMPLETED] This study compared three teaching methods for training resident physicians in lumbar puncture, a critical medical procedure used to collect spinal fluid for diagnosing conditions like meningitis. One hundred thirty-five residents were randomly assigned to either traditional bedside teaching, peer-assisted learning (where trainees practiced in pairs and gave each other feedback), or artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted training using a smart simulator that provided real-time voice feedback on technique. All residents were tested immediately after training and again three months later to see how well they retained their skills. Right after training, all three groups performed equally well. However, after three months, both the peer-learning and AI groups scored significantly higher on practical skills than the traditional group, showing that these newer methods help slow skill decay. The AI group showed the greatest advantages in procedural standardization, pre-procedure assessment, post-procedure care, and operating speed. Meanwhile, residents in the peer-learning group reported the highest satisfaction with classroom interaction and teaching methods. In short, while all three approaches work well for short-term training, AI-assisted and peer-assisted learning are more effective than traditional teaching at helping residents maintain their lumbar puncture skills over time, with AI excelling in technical precision and efficiency, and peer learning offering a more engaging and collaborative learning experience.

title: Artificial Intelligence-assisted Primary Care for Influenza Vaccination Among Chronic Patients in China (AIPC-Flu)
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Fudan University; conditions: Influenza Vaccination; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 1300; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether an AI-assisted primary care intervention can increase influenza vaccination uptake among patients with chronic diseases and to assess the cost-effectiveness and potential for implementing the intervention in routine primary care. The main questions it aims to answer are: 1. Does the AI-assisted primary care intervention increase influenza risk perception, influenza vaccine literacy, vaccine confidence, intention to receive influenza vaccination, and influenza vaccination uptake among patients with chronic diseases? 2. Is the AI-assisted primary care intervention cost-effective compared with conventional health education? 3. Is the AI-assisted primary care intervention acceptable, feasible, and potentially sustainable for influenza vaccination promotion? Researchers will compare patients with chronic diseases who receive the AI-assisted primary care intervention with those who do not receive it to determine whether the intervention improves patients' literacy, confidence, intention, and uptake of influenza vaccination. Participants will: 1. Be recruited and randomly assigned to the intervention group or control group. Participants in the intervention group will have access to an AI assistant for influenza vaccine-related information and will receive an influenza vaccination recommendation from primary care physicians, while participants in the control group will receive routine health education. 2. Complete a survey questionnaire assessing patients' influenza risk perception, influenza vaccine literacy, vaccine confidence, and intention to receive influenza vaccination. 3. Have their influenza vaccination uptake assessed at the end of the trial.
